text.p: --Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette analyst Alex To removed Amgen Inc from the firm's "recommened" list, but continues to have a "buy" recommendation on the stock, To's office confirmed.
--To said he still views Amgen as a "momentum" stock, but not as a "value" stock in view of its recent appreciation.

--In January, when Amgen was trading in the mid-50s, To issued a 12-month price target of $70 on the stock. "On that basis, it is no longer a value stock," he said, citing the share's recent rise as high as 69-3/8.
--To said there is still a chance Amgen shares will pass the $70 mark, but buying the stock at its current price is considerably more risky than when it was $10 cheaper.

--Amgen is due in June to report long-awaited safety data on trials of leptin, the so-called weight-loss protein. To said that in the unlikely event the data is "overwhelmingly negative," Amgen's stock could retrace all of its gains of the year to date. He also said it is unclear how the market would respond to data that showed the compound was safe but said nothing about its efficacy. He said any indication that leptin was effective in producing weight loss would likely be worth some appreciation in the share price. Phase I trials are designed to test safety but often reveal details about a compound's efficacy as well.
"The most likely outcome is that Amgen will report the compound is safe," said To. "The question is, will the market be satisfied with that?"
